svg.title: How a thread is wired into the ThreadManager
svg.desc: Clients call Manager::Spawn with a job and Options to create named workers: AsyncDirector creates four AI buckets, the dev console creates stress workers. The Manager owns a supervisor jthread and a vector of Worker objects addressed by stable WorkerId. On entry every worker thread names itself to the OS and registers with the allocation, profile and diagnostics registries, whose storage is owned by the registry rather than being thread-local so that a force-terminated thread still leaves its evidence behind. The main thread initializes the same registries but is not a managed worker.
svg.text: 1 · CLIENTS — everything threaded is a client of the one registry
ai::AsyncDirector
ai.bucket0 .. ai.bucket3
one worker per IQ bucket · 251/499/997/1999 ms
watchdog 100 ms · autoRestart · priority −1
DevConsole — stress workers
demo.worker · demo.wedged
cancellable long tick · one that ignores its token
watchdog 200 ms · the hard-Kill test case
Spawn(job, Options) → WorkerId
2 · THE MANAGER — owned by Game, declared BEFORE m_world so it outlives every client
m_supervisor : std::jthread
polls every 100 ms, in 10 ms stop-checked slices
reboots a Running tick whose beat > 5 × watchdogMs
skips userStopped / non-autoRestart workers
m_workers : vector<unique_ptr<Worker>>
stable WorkerId from m_nextId — NOT the index,
so Reap() can drop dead slots and survivors
keep the ids the console already showed
m_mx guards the VECTOR STRUCTURE only · per-worker controlMx serialises Stop/Kill/Restart · m_globalScale scales every cadence
Lock order: m_mx → sleepMx. Inspect() and SnapshotAll() read atomics only, so a readout can never block a running worker.
A Worker's std::jthread member is declared LAST, so destruction joins it FIRST — while the fields its loop still touches are alive.
3 · THREAD ENTRY — Manager::Run(w, st), before the first tick
SetOsThreadName(w->name)
debuggers and profilers show the name, not a TID
alloc::RegisterThread(w->name)
prof::RegisterThread(w->name)
diag::RegisterThread(w->name)
registered HERE, so every managed thread is covered
alloc g_entries[64]
constinit — touched from inside operator new
prof slots[16]
a thread holds a POINTER to registry storage
diag ring[N] ← phase 1
the health record this thread will write into
REGISTRY-OWNED STORAGE, never thread_local — and it is a safety property, not tidiness. Kill() force-terminates with
TerminateThread, which runs no destructors and releases the thread's TLS block underneath it. A table of pointers INTO TLS would
be left holding a dangler that the next read follows — in diagnostic code, on the path you reach for when something is already wrong.
The main thread is NOT a managed worker
It calls alloc::Init() and prof::Init() and runs the frame loop itself — no slot, no watchdog, no catch. That is the phase-2 gap.
